limitations: Local geometric terrain visibility only; not certified illumination/power or DSN telecom availability.
Single ray per 0.5 deg azimuth bin at the bin centre; sub-bin peaks can be missed.

Near field PGDA 85 hybrid MLA+SfS DEM 125 m to the inscribed radius of its footprint (<= 12.5 km at 25 m steps), then 125 m steps with PGDA 85 preferred where it has data and MLA GDR v2 250 m elsewhere.
MLA polar GDRs are interpolated between laser tracks (GMT surface); see data_density for the shot coverage.
Horizons az/el (ellipsoid normal) rotated to the sphere normal used by the skyline (<= 0.008 deg).
The MLA/MESSENGER body-fixed prime meridian vs Horizons IAU_MERCURY is not tied (see validation_status).
Hourly samples, no bisection refinement of crossings; no Mercury libration or topography-dependent thermal effects.
Comms: geometric Earth visibility and the SEP-angle outage rule only; threshold is an ENGINEERING ASSUMPTION from DSN 810-005 module 106.
Requirements are the Moon team requirements copied as ENGINEERING ASSUMPTIONS; no Mercury mission requirement exists.
A single rule-selected point is not a surveyed landing site.

world.shape: sphere R = 2 439 400 m for heights and rays (IAU 2015 mean radius; the MLA/USGS map-projection sphere). MLA hdem_75n_250m heights are relative to 2 440 000 m and are re-referenced (+600 m).

conjunctions.source: DSN Telecommunications Link Design Handbook 810-005, module 106 "Solar Corona and Solar Wind Effects", Rev. B (30 Sep 2010), section 2.3: standard downlink BPSK link design and coding achieve X-band data return at SEP angles down to at least 2.3 deg, and Ka-band down to 1 deg. https://deepspace.jpl.nasa.gov/dsndocs/810-005/106/106B.pdf
conjunctions.label: ENGINEERING ASSUMPTION
conjunctions.note: Outage = superior conjunction with SEP below the X-band threshold (coronal scintillation, module 106). Inferior conjunctions below the threshold put the Sun near the ground antenna beam (noise, module 105): flagged, not assessed, not counted as outage.

comms.not_modelled: DSN station elevation and scheduling, link budget, Sun-in-beam noise at inferior conjunction, spacecraft antenna pointing.
